summary: A Set stores each value once and checks membership in O(1) on average. JavaScript compares objects in a Set by identity, so you key by a primitive id to treat equal students as duplicates.
notes: new Set([...]) uses SameValueZero: 1042 equals 1042, but two separate Student objects are never equal, even with the same data.
attendance.set(s.studentId, s) keys the Map by a number, so the second Maya replaces the first instead of adding a new entry.
intersection() returns a new Set with the ids found in both sets. It is new in Node 22 and current browsers.
pitfall: Putting objects in a Set and expecting duplicates to collapse gives no error. The set keeps both Mayas and has() returns false for a new Maya object, because writing an equals() method does not change how Set compares.
contrast: Python and Java let a class define its own hashing with __hash__/__eq__ or hashCode()/equals(). JavaScript has no such hook: Set and Map compare objects by identity, so you key them by a string or number id.
